description: Tessera-wire container, served by Tessera's OWN vLLM plugin: package `tessera.serving`, entry point `tessera = "tessera.serving:register"` under [project.entry-points."vllm.general_plugins"], registering quant_method = "tessera". PrismaQuant never vendors the serving runtime; the boundary crosses through prismaquant/tessera_runtime/tessera_serving_runtime_pin.json and the contract the plugin packages (tessera/serving/runtime_contract.json). THERE IS NO ENABLE FLAG: the checkpoint's `quantization_config.quant_method: "tessera"` selects the plugin, and the single operator knob is TESSERA_SERVE_MODE=resident|streamed, which is declared rather than defaulted because it changes the footprint the artifact occupies and is folded into vLLM's compile-cache key. The serve installs the plugin into the vanilla vLLM image with `pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e <tessera>`; no vLLM patch, no forked runtime. The reference serve script is /home/rob/tessera/experiments/tessera_plugin_served.sh and the route census is /home/rob/tessera/tools/tessera_route_census.py -- both live in the Tessera repository, which this repository does not vendor, so they are NAMED here and not copied.
wired_architectures_note: qwen3 is the profile whose two fused groups Tessera's exporter stacks one-blob-per-vLLM-module, and whose 0.6B checkpoint was served from a PrismaQuant allocation on the plugin (2026-09-02). Moved here from tests/test_profile_export_lanes.py's TESSERA_WIRED on 2026-09-03: the roster is a decision and belongs beside the lane it decides. Declaring the lane is not permission to build one -- the preflight still refuses on the PENDING release pin.

gates.description: Fresh vanilla vLLM container with the pinned Tessera plugin editable-installed, TP=1, speculative decode off, --enforce-eager, then greedy completions over the OpenAI endpoint. Repeat for TESSERA_SERVE_MODE=streamed: the two residencies decode the same bytes by different paths, so an eager receipt in one mode is not a receipt for the other.

A second fresh container under vLLM's default compiled forward and CUDA graphs. Eager success cannot stand in for compiled load/capture/generation success on this lane in particular: the compile-cache identity key has to carry the residency mode, and a mode-blind key is only visible under capture.

Principle 12's second leg on this lane: the per-module route histogram the serve actually emitted, read from the plugin's own telemetry, compared against the artifact's priced activation_contracts. A bpp or KL number whose units rode a route other than the one they were priced on is not a result. The tool lives in the Tessera repository and is named, not vendored. THIS GATE CARRIED `shipcard_slot: null` UNTIL 2026-09-03, which meant the one principle-12 check this lane declares was recorded nowhere and could be refused on by nothing -- the exact `named but never run` shape RobTand/prismaquant#119 describes. It is now a lane-scoped required slot (shipcard.LANE_SCOPED_SLOTS), opened by the arm and refused on by publish_artifact until a real census closes it. The census closes via `python -m prismaquant.shipcard_cli fill-route-census`, which verify replays from the carried records; a serve that ran on the substitute decoder refuses there (PrismaQuant #136).
Unchanged from the native lane: same validator, same endpoint kind, same thresholds. The ship gate is runtime-agnostic and always was.

Served exact full-vocab KL-vs-BF16 in the plugin serving env, against an image-matched BF16 teacher. Match extension residency across A/B arms: the NVFP4 route builds one CUDA extension on first use, and loading a CUDA extension shifts allocator addresses.
Direct WikiText PPL on the served Tessera artifact using the exact CPU-materialized, value-closed offline token payload.

producer_tools.description: The ONLY place the `TESSERA_<BASE>_K<arity>_R<rung>` spelling PrismaQuant allocates in is turned into the exporter's (grid, q256). Named, never vendored: a wire recipe with two homes is how the two halves of one format drift apart. It is tested on the Tessera side (tests/test_plan_from_layer_config.py) but lives under experiments/ with no stability promise, so a tidy-up there breaks a shipping lane here.

The ONLY place the Tessera wire is written. Also tested on the Tessera side, but only by path-loading it (importlib.util.spec_from_file_location in tests/test_serving_export_gate.py, test_export_moe_layouts.py, test_fused_member_rungs.py, test_uniform_control.py) -- which is itself the evidence that it is not an importable entry point. Promotion rides the release-tag commit (RobTand/tessera#17).

The ONLY place the producer states which source tensor, expert, role and geometry each executed routed-expert unit is (schema tessera.expert_projection.v1, with the checkpoint's source_identity). PrismaQuant's campaign asks it once per run for every in-scope MoE stack and prices exactly the units it answers with (prismaquant/tessera_expert_projection.py); the export lane re-binds the allocation to that answer and hands the exporter the priced wires unchanged (--cached-expert-units). Named, never vendored: deriving the projection from tensor names here would be a second home for the producer's packed_expert_weight.

kl_evaluator.note: The producer-side frontier evaluator, reachable because tessera_render renders a Tessera rung through the tessera package: a frontier KL measures the same decode the serve executes. Selection on this lane is SURROGATE by default; nothing here is promoted.

served_activation_quantization.rationale: DERIVED, not hand-asserted (principle 14). Every glob is a formats[] row's `name_pattern` with `{k}` replaced by `*`, read out of the packaged tessera/serving/runtime_contract.json, and each family's A-side contract is the `activation_contract` that same row publishes. TESSERA_E2M1_K2 executes `e2m1_group16_ue4m3_static` -- W4A4: the decoded tile IS the stock NVFP4 tile and the route runs torch._scaled_mm on quantized activations. TESSERA_E4M3_K1 executes `fp8_per_token_dynamic` -- W8A8: the decoded tile is the stock per-channel FP8 pair with per-token dynamic activation scales. TESSERA_BF16_K1 executes `bf16_unquantized` -- W16A16: the decoded tile is a plain bf16 tensor and the route runs the stock BF16 GEMM, so this is the ONE family whose A side genuinely costs nothing, and it says so with a value rather than by omission. That distinction is the reason the field moved onto the formats[] row in Tessera's contract v4: published only on lane_eligibility cells, a family with no receipt yet -- which BF16 is, `attested_rungs_q256` is empty -- had its activation contract in changelog prose, and a consumer could not tell 'unquantised by design' from 'nobody filled it in'. Being listed here is not permission to ship: the eligibility gate reads the CELLS, not this list. As of Tessera contract v5 all three families have cells -- BF16 gained two (sm_121 dense, decode and batch) on the q256=1792 receipt -- so what the gate now refuses is a RUNG outside `attested_rungs_q256`, which is [896] / [1024] / [1792], one point each. Every other rung in every family's reader range still resolves unattested, and that is the rule holding rather than bending.
served_activation_quantization.why_this_matters: The A-side term is what stops the allocator comparing a W4A4 Tessera rung against a W8A8 or a W16A16 one as if the activation side were free. Pricing an A side the runtime does not execute -- or failing to price one it does -- is a CURRENCY error, and it moved a whole 87 GB DSv4 allocation once (2026-08-17, NVFP4_CB). Two of the three families genuinely quantize activations and are priced for it; the third does not, and is priced at 16 bits rather than at zero by default.
served_activation_quantization.if_this_changes: The preflight asserts EQUALITY against the packaged table: tests/test_tessera_lane_admission.py::test_lane_spec_executes_is_derived_from_the_packaged_contract rebuilds this list from tessera/serving/runtime_contract.json and refuses any drift, and the same test pins each family's activation contract. So this field is not maintained by hand -- a runtime that adds a family, retires one, or changes a family's executed contract makes that test fail, and the fix is to re-read the table, never to edit this list to silence it.

notes: ADMISSION IS FAIL-CLOSED UNTIL A TESSERA RELEASE TAG EXISTS. prismaquant/tessera_runtime/tessera_serving_runtime_pin.json carries PENDING sentinels for commit and version, version_is_release is false, and require_exact_tessera_runtime_release refuses them -- so tessera_lane_attested answers False for every rung and no allocation can select one. Cutting the tag is Rob's decision and resolves the pin file and the reader's release constants in one reviewed commit; nothing else in this repository flips the answer.

DENSE-ONLY. The packaged contract declares structures: ["dense"] and carries no routed_moe cell, because no served measurement covers routed experts. Absence is the honest state, not a refusal to serve; the plugin refuses routed MoE by name rather than degrading it.

TP=1 ONLY. The contract's tensor_parallel units both declare max_world_size 1: a Tessera unit is one blob per vLLM module against a shared rate schedule, so a sharded form needs per-rank wires rather than a byte range. expert_parallel.units is empty for the same reason routed MoE is absent.
Both residency modes (TESSERA_SERVE_MODE=resident|streamed) are receipted by the contract's cells and must both be exercised: they decode the same bytes by different paths.
Gates are ADVISORY on this lane as on every other (R16's open half is deferred to Robert); the shipcard is what refuses.

THE ARM EXISTS AND VENDORS NOTHING. `EXPORT_CONTAINER=tessera` in run-pipeline.sh translates layer_config.json into a plan and encodes it by calling TESSERA's own tools under $TESSERA_REPO (experiments/plan_from_layer_config.py, experiments/export_tessera_serving.py), the same named-not-vendored boundary this spec already uses for tessera_plugin_served.sh and tools/tessera_route_census.py. export_native_compressed.py still has no Tessera codec and must not grow one: a wire recipe with two homes is how the two halves of one format drift apart. The arm's preflight is prismaquant/tessera_export_lane.py (declared structure, principle-14 executes derivation, release pin) and it refuses today on the pin alone -- so this spec's bar is now something a run reaches rather than something only a future exporter is built against.
